sentences.text: Shri Ujjawal Vaidya, learned counsel for appellant.
Ms. Shweta Yadav, learned Deputy Advocate General for  respondent/State.

Heard on I.A.No.26006/2025, which is first application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to appellant No.1- Durgeshwar @ Durgesh Sulakhe and appellant No.2- Dharmendra @ Chintu.
The appellants are aggrieved of the judgment dated 28.10.2025 passed by the Special Judge (POCSO) Act, Balaghat Jabalpur in SC No.08/2023, whereby appellant No.1- Durgeshwar @
Durgesh Sulakhe and appellant No.2- Dharmendra @ Chintu have been convicted and sentenced as under:-
Conviction (For Appellant Sentence No.1) Imprisonment in Section Act Imprisonment Fine lieu of fine R.I. for 363 & 366 I.P.C. 7 years R.I. Rs.2,000/-
one months IPC & 376 (2)(n) R.I. for two POCSO 20 years R.I. Rs.3,000/-
 r/w 5(L)/6   Act  Conviction  Sentence  2 Sentence   (For Appellant  No.2)

1  
 Section Act Imprisonment Fine  
 
 363 & 366 I.P.C. 7 years R.I. Rs.2,000/-
 
 POCSO   17 20 years R.I. Rs.3,000/-
 Act  Learned counsel for the appellant submits Chintu is innocent and there are no allegations of commission of rape on appellant No.2 Dharmendra @ Chintu.

It is submitted that as far as appellant No.1/Durgeshwar @ Durgesh Sulakhe is concerned, PW/1 and PW/2 both have stated that mother of PW/1 wanted to marry with Durgeshwar and if Durgeshwar would have accepted this proposal, then report could not have been lodged.
It is also submitted that even in the FIR there is no allegation in regard to violation of privacy.
Ms. Shweta Yadav, learned Deputy Advocate General for State submits that DNA report (Ex.P/28) is positive for Durgeshwar @ Durgesh whereas it is negative for Dharmendra @ Chintu.
It is also submitted that victim's age is less than 18 years and she was not a consenting party.
Her dakhil kharij register, etc., are available on record.
Taking these facts into consideration, we are of the opinion that Dharmendra @ Chintu can be extended benefit of suspension of sentence.

Accordingly, I.A.No.26006/2025 is allowed (in respect of appellant No.2-Dharmendra @ Chintu).
3 CRA-10616-2025

It is directed that on depositing of fine amount, if not already deposited and on furnishing personal bond to the tune of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with two solvent sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for her appearance before the trial Court 26.02.2026 and on all subsequent dates as may be fixed by the concerned Court, the execution of remaining part of the jail sentence of appellant No.2 Dharmendra @ Chintu shall remain suspended and he be released on bail till final disposal of this appeal.
As far as Durgeshwar @ Durgesh Sulakhe is concerned, counsel for appellant prays for withdrawal of I.A. No.26006/2025 qua Durgeshwar @ Durgesh Sulakhe.
Accordingly, I.A. is dismissed as withdrawn qua Durgeshwar @ Durgesh.
List for final hearing in due course.

(VIVEK AGARWAL) (RATNESH CHANDRA SING  JUDGE JUDGE Durgeshwar @ Durgesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69511162/
